text:
Anya: Morning — quick RFC follow-up. I want to propose a 'graft & harvest' approach to long-term refactor: extract tiny, well-scoped adapter grafts around hotpath boundaries, stabilize them for 2–3 sprints, then harvest the old monolith code. TL;DR: less risk, incremental ownership, faster rollback.
Mike: Can you sketch phases?
Anya: Phase 1: Identify 6 low-risk edges (enrichment, session stitch, tenant routing). Build graft services that proxy + translate to existing runtime. Phase 2: Move tests and observability to graft; shadow traffic. Phase 3: Flip traffic + prune code.
Sam: How are we handling stateful pieces (session store, kv-cache)? grafts will be stateless proxies?
Anya: Yes — grafts should be stateless by default. For stateful edges, use sidecar pattern: graft proxies to existing state backend for now. No DB schema changes in Phase 1.
Jess: Product: what's the customer impact window? Need to call out any degraded features.
Anya: Aim for zero customer-visible regressions. We'll schedule small canaries outside peak windows and keep fallback to monolith. Rollout plan uses feature-flag + weighted routing.
Raj: Model-serving concern: latency sensitive paths (inference prefix & kv cache). Any kernel/quantization changes will be orthogonal, but graft latency < 5ms added target?
Mike: 5ms is tight. Our current proxy TLS + serialization adds ~3ms. Want to budget 10ms worst-case.
Anya: Agree. Budget 10ms. We'll add batching knobs at graft layer for non-critical calls and bypass for low-latency paths.
Sam: Observability: tracer/span continuity must survive the handoff. Plan to propagate trace ids and add a shim extractor in the graft.
Anya: Correct. We'll adopt the runtime's trace header X-Request-Trace and emit a preflight span.
Mike: Who owns the graft services? Team assignment?
Anya: Initial owners: eng-runtime owns graft templates + infra; downstream service teams own specific grafts. We'll add a one-month rotation owner if no clear team.
Jess: Testing & CI? Integration smoke should run against both graft and monolith in shadow mode.
Anya: We'll add a dedicated job `graft-smoke` in CI that runs end-to-end against staging with 3 traffic profiles. Example curl to validate routing:
```bash
curl -H \"X-Feature: graft-tenant-routing\" \"https://staging.graft.example/api/v1/route?tenant=acme\"
```
Sam: Nice. Need a synthetic that asserts no token-cost regression too.
Raj: For model-profile registry interactions, graft should use read-only cached copy and fall back to control-plane API. Avoid adding write paths.
Mike: DB migrations? If we eventually remove fields, we should do a two-step safe-delete: stop writes -> read-only window -> prune.
Anya: Agreed. We'll add explicit migration RFC per table. No destructive changes in the initial harvest.
Jess: Rollback story?
Anya: Feature-flag off + immediate traffic switch to monolith. Also keep a quick path exec `scripts/flip-traffic.sh` to flip weights.
Mike: Can we add a safety gate in console to flip per-tenant?
Anya: Yes — the Console team will expose per-tenant weight controls (UI + API).
Sam: Observability: add SLO delta alerts for p50/p95 token latency and error rate.
Anya: We'll set temporary SLOs: p95 increase <= 20% and error rate < 0.1% during canary, else auto-rollback.
Raj: Security review? grafts must go through threat model and KMS review if they touch keys.
Anya: Security will review pre-Phase 1 merges. No new key material in grafts initially.
Mike: Timelines?
Anya: Kickoff next Monday. Phase 1 (grafts) 3 sprints; Phase 2 (stabilize) 2 sprints; Phase 3 (harvest) 4+ sprints depending on complexity.
Jess: Dependencies: console controls, CI jobs, tracing shim. Who's tracking tasks?
Anya: I'll own the main epic and create sub-epics for each graft. Will assign leads in the first planning meeting.
Sam: One more: perf testing harness must simulate batching & KV cache warm/cold.
Anya: Good call — add to perf team TODOs.
Mike: Sounds reasonable. +1 to incremental approach.
Jess: +1 from product.
Raj: +1 from ML. We should flag any model rollout dependencies early.
Anya: I'll post a follow-up RFC doc with sequence diagrams and a checklist. Thanks.
deploy-bot: Canary started for graft-tenant-routing on staging (job id: graft-canary-202603).
deploy-bot: Canary metrics: p50 +2ms, p95 +9ms, errors 0.03% — within gates.
